industry.semaMarketsNote: IQVIA 2025 sales (US$m) and units (m) of the innovator's semaglutide in markets going off patent by H1-2026, as shown in OneSource's Q4FY26 deck (p.8); OneSource partners hold ~2/3 of the generic injectable market by value in India (Apr-2026)
timing: Exclusivity lapsed Jan-2026; Health Canada approved Dr Reddy's and a second partner (Orbicular's licensee) in Apr-May-2026; both launched; Dr Reddy's paused supply on 9-Jul-2026 after an API impurity and guided a resumption in a few months
Patent expired Mar-2026; multiple OneSource customers launched on day one; ~40% of generic pens sold in Jun-2026 made by OneSource; monthly generic pens rose from <2,000 to 150,000-160,000
Patent expired Mar-2026; ANVISA reviewing ~17 applicants; OneSource's site is ANVISA-approved; customers expected in the first wave
Several customer filings; approvals over FY27
Orbicular (OneSource partner) has USFDA tentative approval; launch on patent expiry (~2031-32); two customers hold first-to-file status for generic tirzepatide
Opens ~2031 ('29-30 onwards' per management, FY29-30 fiscal)
industry.timingSrc: Q4FY26 deck and call (13-May-2026); Q1FY27 call (25-Jul-2026); Dr Reddy's BSE filing 9-Jul-2026 (Fierce Pharma, Medical Dialogues); DAM Capital (30-Jun-2025) for the US launch year
industry.biologics: Biologics and DDC are the fastest-growing CDMO segments globally (CEO); new USFDA/EU biosimilar guidance cuts development cost and time; BIOSECURE Act and NDAA 2026 push work from China; India's biologics CDMO share is small vs South Korea
industry.competition: Fill-finish and device assembly for generic GLP-1s: Indian generic majors building own capacity, global CDMOs and device makers; a listed peer is expanding from 40m to 140m devices (Q2FY26 call); OneSource's customers have first right of refusal to match prices in markets like Canada (Chairman, Jan-2026)

brokers.thesis: Moving from order-book build to commercial execution in DDC; only CDMO with G7 semaglutide approvals; sterile days to triple to 675 in FY28; biologics a second engine from FY29; FY27E EBITDA cut 3.6%, FY28E raised 6.5%; four-month injectables shutdown a near-term drag

Pick of the week: fully booked GLP-1 capacity on take-or-pay and reservation fees; cartridges 40m to 220m; acquisition adds US$100m revenue; method not stated (target = 24.3x its FY28E EPS); before the Q3FY26 miss

2QFY26 beat on MSA execution; 40%/52% organic revenue/EBITDA CAGR FY25-28E; capacity pulled forward; Canadian delays may shift launches. Earlier (6-May-2025): Rs2,113 on 22x 1QFY28E EBITDA with FY27E revenue Rs2,640 cr, EBITDA Rs1,040 cr, EPS Rs62.1. No later note found

Initiation: differentiated multi-platform specialty CDMO; first mover in DDC; revenue/EBITDA/adjusted PAT CAGR 33%/42%/60% FY25-28E; ~40% adjusted ROCE; US generic Wegovy profit share from 2032. No later note found
Initiation: ~20 GLP-1 partnerships on scarce fill-finish capacity; EBITDA to roughly triple FY25-28; DDC ~50% of FY27E EBITDA; main risk approval delays. No later note found

blocks: Tenshi Pharmaceuticals (promoter), Pronomz Ventures (promoter group) and Medella Holdings

moat.factor: First-mover GLP-1 DDC capacity and approvals
moat.evidence: Filling partner for all three Canadian and the first G7 semaglutide approvals; 20+ DDC customers; end-to-end fill, inspect, assemble, pack
210+ audits without failure; USFDA (CDER and CDRH), EU GMP, ANVISA, Health Canada, TGA approvals across sites
Each customer's product is filed on OneSource's site; changing site needs new filings, but batch-size and site changes are 'annual reportable' in many markets and customers can dual-source
Biologics DS+DP on one site, DDC, sterile injectables and soft gels; cross-selling (50+ customers on 2+ projects); but biologics is early and soft gel was captive to Strides
One cartridge line until Q2FY27; ~Rs1,400 cr revenue; competitors (generic majors, global CDMOs) are adding capacity; pricing becomes a factor once capacity is no longer scarce
Two customers 31.9% of FY26 revenue; Strides group entities ~28%; semaglutide demand depends on a few partners' approvals and supply (Dr Reddy's API halt)

critiques: Guidance credibility: FY26 was guided at ~30% growth and fell 2%; the FY28 target has been held for two years while the acquisition-inclusive version was raised and then withdrawn
Earnings are tiny against the price: reported PAT was a loss in FY25 and FY26 and Rs25 cr in Q1FY27; the stock trades on FY28 hopes
Generic semaglutide prices are falling fast in India; as more fill-finish capacity arrives, CDMO pricing power may fade once capacity is no longer scarce

Related-party intensity: ~28% of revenue from Strides-group entities, conversion and support payments to Strides and Arcolab, a proposed related-party acquisition that minorities pushed back on, and 37% of promoter shares pledged
Working capital ballooned (receivables 177 days, inventory Rs439 cr) and covenants were waived for FY26; debt rises with capex before EBITDA arrives
A US$136m arbitration claim (Prestige, Sputnik vaccine) is not provided for
Company 'adjusted PAT' adds back the gross scheme amortisation and ignores its tax effect
